issue.title: BM25 indexes reject valid NUMERIC typmods with |scale| > 18

relevant_locations.role: Extracts precision and scale from PostgreSQL NUMERIC typmod
Provides alternative numeric bytes representation for wide precision or scales
Handles numeric bound scaling based on selected field type

llm_context.input_title: BM25 indexes reject valid NUMERIC typmods with |scale| > 18
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: PostgreSQL NUMERIC(precision, scale) columns with |scale| > 18 fail when building a BM25 index or initializing an empty index due to the representation-selection logic incorrectly choosing Numeric64 even when the scale exceeds the bounds supported by Decimal64NoScale (-18 through 18).
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: `SearchFieldType::try_from_type_info` or equivalent configuration builders inspect precision to choose `Numeric64` but fail to validate that the absolute scale is within the 18-scale limit mandated by `Decimal64NoScale`.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect extract_numeric_precision_scale and representation selection
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect extract_numeric_precision_scale in pg_search/src/postgres/utils.rs and the field configuration builders in pg_search/src/schema/config.rs to understand how precision and scale are currently evaluated for choosing Numeric64 versus NumericBytes.

step_by_step_plan.title: Update numeric representation selection logic for scale bounds
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the schema configuration logic to verify that not only is precision <= 18, but the absolute scale (|scale| <= 18) is also within the supported range of Decimal64NoScale before selecting Numeric64; otherwise, fall back to NumericBytes.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add a regression test for NUMERIC with scale > 18
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a new test case to the test suite that defines a table with a NUMERIC(precision, scale) column where precision <= 18 but scale > 18 (e.g., NUMERIC(10, 20)), initializes a BM25 index on it, and verifies that index creation and queries succeed without failing on Decimal64NoScale range limits.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run test suite verification
step_by_step_plan.description: Run cargo test to verify that all existing tests pass and the new regression test correctly validates the wide scale NUMERIC field mapping.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: PostgreSQL encodes column precision and scale metadata into an integer called a typmod.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Extensions must correctly decode typmods to understand the decimal constraints and numeric ranges defined by users.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The issue stems from correctly extracting the scale but failing to validate it against the limits of the chosen backend encoder.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Choice between fast 64-bit integer storage (Numeric64) and flexible byte-encoded storage (NumericBytes) for decimals.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Numeric64 offers high performance but has strict precision and scale boundaries (-18 to 18), whereas NumericBytes supports arbitrary precision and scale.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The selection logic must evaluate whether the column's scale exceeds 18 so it can fall back to NumericBytes instead of crashing in Decimal64NoScale.

common_pitfalls: Forgetting that PostgreSQL scales can be negative (e.g., rounding to tens or hundreds), meaning the check must use absolute scale (|scale| > 18).
Modifying query execution paths without updating schema generation logic.
